author: Timeline15
text:
Fights were all pretty quick. Still impressive, but I hope we get a couple of three minute slugfests before the season is over.
Magnitude remains super impressive. Disarray sadly wasn't fully functional from the off. God I wish Claw Viper had been able to make it, but props to Disarray for doing the best they could.
Switchback hits so much harder now, and their beater was robust enough to shatter Ribbot's and still just about hold together. It can't be used again, but it got them to the end of the fight. Great to see how the bot's evolved over the last few years.
Great to see Terrortops get a win over a heavy hitter like Valkyrie. Durability was the main thing I was unsure about with them, and their wedge held up super well. The weapon also hits surprisingly hard for something that shares weight/space with a lifter. Like Switchback, they've also come a long way quite quickly; one wonders what the bot will be like in another couple of years.
I will say though, the pre-fight content for Valkyrie was a little weird.
The show tried to set up this tension about whether the parts would get delivered, but the editing is so fast that we get the answer mere seconds later. It's just like "our parts didn't come - oh!, they're here! But they're made wrong - oh! We fixed it!" Just kinda too many steps to cram into such a concise format.
Overall a better episode than last week, though I'm still waiting for a big stand-out moment that really makes the season memorable.

episode: The World’s Toughest Robot Tournament Begins | BATTLEBOTS PRO LEAGUE EP 1 | POWERED BY BRIGHT DATA
author: GrahamCoxon
text:
That episode was fine, which is a problem because it needed to be better than fine with the material the teams gave them to work with. It took 2 and a half good fights and failed to do them justice by presenting them poorly in ways that were entirely within their control and avoidable.
I'd like to talk positives first, though. The fights were good; they didn't pad the runtime with a  bunch of fluff and instead added just enough decent-quality BTS stuff; and most importantly they're running a genuinely good judging system. Hopefully Damage & Engagement being used here helps encourage EOs to use it more widely.
Getting back to the overall episode quality, however, there are some glaring things that just seem to point to a lack of care. They're mixing broadcast-quality camerawork with blurry, shaky action-cam shots that stick out like a sore thumb. They're crash-zooming and cropping in digitally on a bunch of shots for absolutely no reason, making their long-form episode feel like a short made by teenagers for teenagers. They're also just generally cutting hyperactively, with bundles of dizzyingly short shots cut together quickly for no discernable reason – often using bizarre transitions for extra unmotivated and unwanted disorientation. The intro was maybe the worst example, with an onslaught of quick shots for some reason cutting back to equally short shots of Chris just talking because...what...they worried we would forget he was there?
While they do manage to slow this down a bit during fights, there are still a lot of needless and distracting cuts. Did nobody at any point question the value and purpose of a 1 second cutaway to a heavily zoomed/cropped Kenny finishing a sentence? NHRL cuts fights live, in real-time, and still creates fights where cuts rarely actively detract from the watchability of the fight. Maybe that's one small part of why they attract more concurrent viewers to a slower-paced stream of a live event than Battlebots pull to the premier of a season premier.
Overall I just have absolutely no idea who is trying to impress who with the edit – its a thankfully less extreme version of ViV all over again.
But, overall, praise be to our overlords – the brightest of datas – for really digging into the...data...and excavating the nugget of gold that is 'fans online think that HUGE will beat the robot they believed was coming into the fight as a fairly standard meta vert'. No human could have done that, so big up Brizzle Dizzle for taking time out of their busy schedule of facilitating cyberattacks on human rights groups to really chew on that one for us.

Cobalt versus The Twins:
that was one of the most cautious battles I've seen in a while. I am especially impressed that one if The Twins took a direct hit from Cobalt's weapon and wasn't dead afterwards. Those are tough little robots.
Minotaur versus Bloodsport:
very good driving by Minotaur, picking their shots and hitting the corners of Bloodsport to take out their wheels. Expensive damage to Bloodsport, completely wrecked one of their expensive billet frames.
Orbitron versus Witch Doctor:
surprisingly bad driving from Orbitron, they seemed more interested in ramming the walls than attacking their opponent. Of course Witch Doctor made short work of them, you don't make that kind of driving error in front of a top team and survive.
My wife watched that fight with me, and she thought that Orbitron's AI was confused by the high-contrast stripes on Witch Doctor. I doubt that was the cause of their poor driving, but it would be amusing if dazzle camouflage turned out to be the key to defeating an AI opponent.

author: MudnuK
text:
That was good.. I think? It was such a whirlwind I'm not entirely sure WHAT I saw. I even missed that the judging criteria have changed.
But of what I managed to process, good fights. Interesting they lead with
a fight that ended with both weapons going down but the aggression
kept it interesting.
The editing is mind-meltingly choppy. People were worried about having only 3 fights in a 30-minute episode but this could have been 45 minutes easily, with a slower pace, better build-up and more pit time. The pacing was just so rushed I felt like I was watching a stream of highlights. And so many unneeded cuts and zooms. The last two FaceOffs did it better.
EDIT: The Team Witch Doctor behind the scenes episodes from FaceOffs were everything this should have been.
The sponsorships were hardly subtle but I was relieved they didn't take over. I'm happy with that balance if it brings in the funding.
Deathroll vs Golden Fury
Deathroll took the first punch well. I feel they could have been a little more confident in taking chances to catch Golden Fury on the sides/back but the opportunities were brief. Happy to see GF last the distance, and I know there's more to be seen of that weapon. Deathroll likely missed their best chance for a win in this group and I wonder if they toned the weapon down a touch. Shame it didn't work in the end. But it kept fighting, the srimech worked great, lots of positives. E: Golden Fury's drive looks powerful.
Hypershock vs HUGE
Well done to the Hypershock team, as the config worked! Immediately took out a drive side's worth of belts on HUGE. But they seemed to get sort of tangled in the corner rather than picking their shots, and though I mostly missed it, HUGE managed to get shots to the sides even with their drive half gone. I wonder if this victory is actually the weakest HUGE will look all season, with that damage? Hard to think what could bring them down.
Malice vs End Game
It all hinged on that fork. And the trouble with barbed forks is you can't release. The other trouble is that they can come off. Sucks that End Game's weapon went down immediately and they did great without it, but the two getting stuck together meant (ironically) that End Game gave Malice a bit of space upon untangling and the horizontal got their angle. Well done to them to keep a level head going for that srimech, though it didn't look like it was working anyway. Big upset and Malice has again earned my respect.

episode: NEW BOT THREATS ARE RISING! | BATTLEBOTS PRO LEAGUE EPISODE 3 | POWERED BY BRIGHT DATA
author: ellindsey
text:
Better fights this week, and the editing wasn't as bad as it had been. I was especially glad to see more shots of the damage breakdown after the fights.
Switchback versus Ribbot: Very good showing from Switchback, although the fight was really over too quickly to see if their reliability issues had really been fixed. They won mostly by having better geometry, managing to get in underneath Ribbot every time they went weapon-to-weapon, and also having a narrower eggbeater precisely sized to smash Ribbot's eggbeater. Good showing from them, let's see if they can keep it up. Ribbot's only real chance here would have been to get Switchback from the side instead of going weapon-on-weapon, but Switchback was too quick to let that happen.
Magnitude versus Disarray: Yeah, Disarray never really stood a chance here. Their weapon wasn't even spinning up at first, and parts of their robot broke off on every time the robots hit each other. They held up longer than I expected them to at least. I don't think that Magnitude is going to have this easy of a time against Madcatter though.
Valkyrie versus Terrortops: Terrortops just owned this fight from the start. Just smacking Valkyrie around the arena, until Valkyrie couldn't move well enough to avoid being counted out. I'm not sure exactly why Valkyrie couldn't move, the wheels seemed to still be moving. Hung up on its own damaged armor, maybe? Possibly had one side of the drivetrain out? I don't blame Terrortops for hanging back and letting Valkyrie be counted out, it's a dangerous robot to hit and they could have freed it up and let it move again if they had hit it. Terrortops has turned into a pretty serious robot.

author: Timeline15
text:
Good fights this episode:
Cobalt vs The Twins:
I am
so
glad to see The Twins win here. Multibots have been so effective in the lower weight classes, but until now that success has never scaled up to heavyweight. Seems Reasonable have finally cracked it though. They had enough ground game to win every front-to-front exchange, enough downforce to not just get bulldozed out of the way, and even enough durability to take a big hit from Cobalt and still be driving when they came back down. We've come a
long
way from Uppercut vs Gemini.
Minotaur vs Bloodpsort:
That went about how I expected. I honestly don't think there's a way to make overhead spinners viable in the modern meta; opponents are just too fast and durable. Minotaur was able to just full send into Bloodsport's bar over and over again and keep stopping it. Not to mention you have to run away every time you need to spin up. I really think the only future for horizontals in designs like RotatoR: spinner at one end, big wedge at the other so you can deflect/push without the blade getting slowed down.
Witch Doctor vs Orbitron:
That was probably one of the worst performances yet out of Orbitron's autonomous control. It doesn't usually take them into walls repeatedly like that. Not really much to say about the new Witch Doctor as it didn't really get challenged much yet. The drive seems pretty slippy, but that may just be the box floor at work.
All in all , probably the best one yet. It was still pacey obviously, but none of the talky parts felt obviously cut to pieces for time like they did in previous weeks.

author: mwidjaja1
text:
I'm not an expert in YouTube's algorithm
There are a lot of indirect and direct reasons 20/30 mins work.
That's the length where, for many creators, it's easy for them to upload videos on a regular basis which builds consistent traffic and growth momentum. It's a length that's long enough to fit enough Ad space in, get your message across, and feel satisfying on the other end.
I posted this elsewhere but remember, to run a 30 min TV Program, that means you need 21-22 mins of content after you account for Ads. Battlebots, to my recent awareness, never had to be placed in a situation where they had to air for just 30 minutes, but that would be the cheapest way to get back on TV/streaming as the smallest duration slot. Figuring out how to do 30 mins well means getting Battlebots into a 21-22 min length.
I suspect if you're a very popular and large creator, the algorithm matters way less than someone trying to get their foot in the door like Battlebots.
